methods.label: Pair the row counts
methods.explanation:
Pairing small and large row counts finds the total without adding every row separately. Add \(1+2+\cdots+N\) to the same sum written in reverse order. There are \(N\) pairs, each totaling \(N+1\), so
\[
2\cdot2016=N(N+1),
\qquad N(N+1)=4032.
\]
The consecutive factors can be found near \(64\):
\[
4032=4096-64=64^2-64=63\cdot64.
\]
Thus \(N=63\) works. Since \(N\) is a positive integer and \(N(N+1)\) strictly increases as \(N\) increases, it is the only possible row count. Its digits sum to \(6+3=9\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Pairing a finite sum and checking consecutive factors requires only elementary arithmetic.
